claims.statement: EU online buyers generally have a 14-day right to cancel and return without justification, subject to exemptions, which makes returns a recurring merchant workflow rather than an optional edge case.
In 2024, 24% of EU enterprises conducted e-sales, but the statistic includes services and lower-volume sellers and does not establish the candidate's target-account count.

EU apparel and footwear rules encourage alternatives to destruction and phase obligations by company size; this can increase demand for disposition records but regulation is available to every vendor and is not defensibility.

Allegro reported 164,000 LTM active verified merchants in Poland as of Q2 2025, but did not disclose how many meet the candidate's physical-goods order-volume, category, data-quality, and budget filters.
Allegro's seller tools now export up to two years of return data with products, value, selected reason, and logistics fields, making basic historical return reporting platform-native.
Shopify exposes stable category-specific return reasons at line-item level, materially improving raw reason data but also lowering the technical barrier for competing analytics apps.

Shopify can record inspected return dispositions including missing, processing required, restocked, and not restocked; reliable observations still depend on merchant or fulfilment staff recording them.
Shopify apps see only the last 60 days of orders by default; older history needs read_all_orders approval and merchant-granted scopes, so a six-to-twelve-month diagnostic cannot assume API access.
AfterShip offers return reasons by SKU and order, analytics, routing, integrations, and an entry plan around $16 monthly, placing a low price anchor under generic returns analytics.

ReasonWhy offers AI return-reason clustering, product ranking by loss impact, recommended page fixes, and before/after tracking for $49-$199 monthly, closely reproducing the candidate's generic root-cause artifact.

Progress Jiu Jitsu reportedly used product-level reason data to change size guidance and manufacturing measurements and saw returns fall from 17% to 7%, showing that at least one merchant acted on recommendations; the vendor case is selected and uncontrolled.

A StrutFit customer case describes a four-month A/B test for an EMEA footwear sizing intervention with lower return rate and positive conversion and order-value effects, showing that causal attribution is operationally possible for a narrow online intervention.

Because platforms and inexpensive apps already provide reasons, rankings, recommendations, and dispositions, generic AI analysis has no scarce control; a viable product must add cross-platform CEE joins, trustworthy physical outcomes, or superior causal measurement.
It is unknown whether CEE merchants consistently record truthful line-level reasons and physical-condition outcomes across marketplaces, storefronts, WMS, 3PL, repair, and liquidation systems.
It is unknown what proportion of target merchants will implement content, sizing, supplier, routing, or disposition recommendations and maintain the required experimental holdout.
Avoided-loss attribution outside a randomised, stepped-wedge, or well-matched cohort design is unknown because seasonality, promotion, assortment, price, and channel mix co-move with returns.

The number of merchants meeting the 5,000-200,000 monthly-order, target-category, data-quality, and willingness-to-pay filters is unknown despite the large Allegro upper bound and broad Eurostat e-sales base.
No current evidence establishes agency, 3PL, or integrator partner commitment, paid conversion, or CAC for the CEE wedge.

Comparable prices support testing 400-1,500 PLN monthly rather than 2,500-12,000 PLN; at 200 customers and 1,000 PLN monthly, 2.4m PLN ARR and a 25% owner-cash margin yield 600,000 PLN per mature year, so the 5m PLN path is slower and still unvalidated.

A batch-first, one-category pilot is compatible with the founder's capital and time, but live multi-platform connectors and merchant-specific analysis can exceed the five-hour daily limit unless onboarding and reviews are standardised.

contrary_evidence: Allegro, Shopify, and return-management vendors already expose return reasons, reports, analytics, and disposition fields.
A new Shopify app directly offers AI reason clustering, product ranking, recommended fixes, and impact tracking at $49-$199 monthly.
Default Shopify history access is only 60 days, so the proposed long diagnostic needs additional approval or exports.
Merchant action and attribution evidence is concentrated in selected vendor apparel and footwear cases rather than independent CEE evidence.
